c5-negative-control.title: Close criterion 5: negative-control (swap) logic
c5-negative-control.imperative: Confirm the swap comparison uses a DIFFERENT session's G than the after comparison. Re-read the code, don't trust the printed table.
c5-negative-control.finding: L304 after=(pa-ga)-(pb-gb) uses each session's OWN G. L306 swap=(pa-gb)-(pb-ga) uses each session's WRONG G (ga,gb swapped). Wired to different G than after; algebraically after=before-(ga-gb), swap=before+(ga-gb). Numerically after_rms 7.715 != swap_rms 8.615 -> not accidentally identical. Directionality evidence is the after<swap ordering (correct correspondence beats wrong), which holds. CONFIRMED correctly wired.

consolidation.summary: Harness is a correctly-measured honest-null, not a flawed-harness artifact. All 8 close criteria + 7 survey checks pass; the +155.5% negative is REAL. Two non-blocking triage candidates (G fit identifiability; sigma-gating).

triage_candidates.statement: G's saturating-curve fit is structurally unidentified on FP-session data (offset<->asymptote corr ~= +/-1, physically absurd asymptotes e.g. Monaco FP2 = -107640s), full-field AND split -- independently reproduced. G is not usable as a cross-session subtractable baseline on practice data as currently fit. Candidate fixes: bound/regularize the asymptote+rate, restrict G to sessions with sufficient cumulative-track-laps spread, or flat-offset fallback when |corr| near 1. (Excluded from this gate per handoff; Commander decides reopen-g2 vs accept-null.)

get_grip_at returns an honestly-inflated sigma for these degenerate fits, but the prescribed reconciliation subtracts only the point estimate mu; a sigma-weighted/sigma-gated consumer would down-weight degenerate corrections. Worth considering whether 'subtract G' should be sigma-gated downstream.
